To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) noisy data is useful in the training of deep neural network models; (2) noisy data is particularly useful for fine-grained recognition tasks; and (3) noisy data can be used to augment the training data for a given task, and this is a viable alternative to collecting more data for a given classi cation task.

(1) we can achieve a signi cant performance boost on FGVC tasks by using a simple, yet powerful, data augmentation scheme; (2) we can achieve further performance boost by training a model on a larger, yet noisy, data set, as long as the training process is carefully designed; (3) our approach can also be used to train models on noisy data with no additional cost.

1) noisy data is a key factor in the success of deep networks, 2) the noise is not just random, but has a strong signal in terms of what is relevant for the task at hand, and 3) the noise is useful in terms of the information it conveys, and not just a nuisance that must be removed.
